node 00
manuscript

Quantum Cramér-Rao bounds for squeezed Fock states under decoherence

J. Park and S. Mouradian, in preparation. Derivation draft dated 2 Nov 2026.

Plain version: a weak force nudges a trapped ion's motion. We read the nudge through the ion's internal qubit. I derived how small a nudge you can resolve when the motion starts in a Fock state |n⟩ with squeezing r, and how cooling, heating and dephasing during the measurement change which state to use.

resultBelow a crossover noise rate, higher Fock states win; above it they lose, and every state falls onto one universal line. For 6.98 ms of exposure the crossovers are 31, 10 and 6 s⁻¹ for n = 1, 2, 3.
resultAt strong dephasing the higher Fock states come back: the dephased drive acts as a hot bath that switches off as dephasing grows. Squeezing helps only when dephasing is weak. Node 04.

node 01
protocol

The sensing protocol in phase space

Prepare the motion, let the signal displace it by β, split the two spin branches by ±α with a spin-dependent force, measure the qubit. The whole measurement reduces to one number, the qubit coherence C = V e−iΦ: Φ carries the signal, V is how much the branches still overlap.

rendered from the same Wigner-function math as the simulations. red positive, blue negative. x is the quadrature the signal moves, p the one the force probes. n = 1, r = 0.3, β = 0.9, α = 1.2.
wigner functionsnumpyffmpeg
node 02
derivation

Closed forms for the bound

  • 02.1Ground state: bound e4α²/16α², minimum e/4 at α = ½.
  • 02.2Squeezed Fock state: overlap V = e−2α²e−2rLn(4α²e−2r). Each quantum adds a node; squeezing rescales α by e−r.
  • 02.3Optimal readout solves Ln − yLn + 2yL′n = 0, independent of r. For n = 1, y = 2 + √3.
  • 02.4Cold bath during the drive: factor (2/Γt)(1 − e−Γt/2) and penalty e4α²(1−e−Γt); thermal bath multiplies the penalty by 2n̄ + 1.
  • 02.5Near zero noise the best bound grows as esΓt, s = (2n̄+1)e2ryn − ½, which gives the crossover rates.
constraintEvery closed form had to be reproduced by a simulation that never saw the formula.
open quantum systemsquantum fisher informationanalytic

Two independent numerical pipelines

A full Lindblad master equation for ion plus mode in IonSim.jl and QuantumOptics.jl, and a stepwise Trotter pipeline that applies drive, dephasing, cooling and heating in slices and evaluates the qubit Fisher information directly.

n = 1, β = 2, pure dephasing 365 Hz. points: master equation. green: stepwise theory. red dotted: noiseless formula. notebook 2026-10-25.

node 04
phase diagram

Which state to prepare, at which noise level

The best Fock state over a heating × dephasing map, at signal β = 1. With weak noise the highest Fock state wins. As dephasing grows, the best state falls to |1⟩ or the vacuum, and then, at strong dephasing, the higher Fock states come back. On the right are the Wigner functions of the state after the noisy signal at the three marked points: clean rings that shift rigidly (①), rings smeared into a disk (②), and rings that return (③).

best n* over Γφt × Γht, hot bath Γc = Γh, β = 1, n ≤ 5. right: W(x, p) after the signal, with each state's min QCRB, rank and Wigner negativity. notebook 1121_dephasing_reentrance, P7.

Why it comes back: under strong dephasing the drive stops acting coherently and works on the populations like a hot bath of strength Γβ = 4β²/Γφt. That bath is strongest when Γφt ~ 4β² and erases the Fock advantage. Past that point it switches off as 1/Γφt, and the signal is read through a contrast term that favours the outer Laguerre lobes only higher Fock states have.

squeezed atlas: hue = n, shade = r ∈ {0, 0.2, 0.4, 1}. hot bath, β = 1. notebook 1121_squeezed_atlas, A.
left: what squeezing buys over the best plain Fock state, in dB. right: best r* (shade) and best n* (lines). notebook 1121_squeezed_atlas, C.
resultSqueezing helps only at weak dephasing: up to 6.4 dB at Γφt ~ 10⁻³–10⁻², under 1 dB near 0.1, and nothing beyond about 1. Dephasing destroys coherences between number states at a rate ∝ (j − k)², and a squeezed state is spread over many of them.
checkRaising the cutoff from 61 to 91 levels, doubling the time steps and widening the readout grid changed the best state at none of 84 test points. The strong-dephasing closed form picks the same n* as the engine on 208 of 220 points; the misses sit on boundaries.

node 06
in progress

Next: one long exposure or many short ones?

The question I am working on now: with a fixed time budget, is it better to read out once after one long exposure, or to split it into short rounds and reset in between? Without noise one long exposure wins. With cooling, heating or dephasing the motion behaves like a leaky integrator, so the displacement saturates and splitting starts to pay. Early closed forms suggest the best split follows constants that do not depend on n; the finite-signal case is not finished.

SQRLab.jl and the lab notebooks

A Julia package on top of IonSim.jl for pulse sequences, Ramsey sweeps and noise models, with a Ref-based trick that compiles the Hamiltonian once per sweep instead of once per point. The dated notebooks behind every figure above are public, including the November ones that map the re-entrance (1121_dephasing_reentrance, 1121_squeezed_atlas) and a separate Python cross-check of the engine.

left: best n* over Γφt × β with no cooling or heating; black dotted lines are the closed-form boundaries, white dashed is Γβ = 0.117. right: gain of n* over the vacuum. notebook 1121_dephasing_reentrance, P1.
